sides.name: Confederate States: Army of Northern Virginia (Lee)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Army 65,000-75,000 (possibly 80,000), 270 guns, ~9,500 cavalry overall. Day 0 (1 July) = divisions of Heth, Pender, Rodes and Early, ~27,000 engaged (Livermore via Martin). Arrivals: day 0.3 (evening 1 July) Anderson and Johnson; day 1.0 (morning 2 July) Hood and McLaws of Longstreet's corps; day 1.5 Stuart's three cavalry brigades (no role on 2 July); day 1.8 Pickett's division (fought 3 July). Divisional strengths and per-arrival gun counts follow Busey & Martin as commonly cited (approximate, not fetched). Weapons 6.5: rifled muskets, mixed rifled/smoothbore artillery. ISR 6.0: Stuart absent until 2 July. Mapped to archetype-gunpowder-linear (linear tactics with rifled muskets). Morale 0.9 after Chancellorsville.

sides.name: United States: Army of the Potomac (Meade)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Army 93,500-104,256, 360 guns. Day 0 (1 July) = I and XI Corps plus Buford's cavalry division, ~22,000 engaged (Livermore via Martin). Arrivals: day 0.3 (evening 1 July) XII Corps and most of III Corps; day 0.9 (night/morning 2 July) II and V Corps, Artillery Reserve, Gregg's and Kilpatrick's cavalry divisions; day 1.65 (afternoon 2 July) VI Corps after a ~30-mile march. Corps strengths follow Busey & Martin as commonly cited (approximate, not fetched); Buford's withdrawal on 2 July and Merritt's brigade on 3 July not modelled. Logistics 6.8: rail-fed. Comms 6.7: telegraph and signal corps. Fortification 6.6: breastworks on Culp's Hill and the fish-hook ridge line (field works, not a fortified city).

outcome.note: Union victory. Union 23,049 (3,155 killed, 14,529 wounded, 5,365 captured or missing). Confederate 23,000-28,000 (Busey & Martin 23,231; higher totals count stragglers captured in the retreat). Day 1 alone: Union ~9,000, Confederate ~6,000. From ~07:30 on 1 July to the end of Pickett's Charge ~16:00 on 3 July (2.4 days); Lee withdrew on 4 July.
